name: Make a basic pan sauce
blurb: The skill that makes a plain piece of meat taste like a restaurant dish, built from what is already stuck to the pan. Five minutes, no recipe needed.
gear: A stainless or cast-iron pan — non-stick does not build fond
steps: Cook the protein in a pan that browns properly and rest it on a warm plate.
Pour off excess fat, leaving the browned bits — the fond — behind.
Sweat a chopped shallot or garlic in the residual fat for a minute.
Deglaze with wine, stock or even water, scraping every bit of fond off the base with a wooden spoon.
Reduce by half to two-thirds until it coats the back of a spoon.
Off the heat, whisk in cold butter a cube at a time to emulsify and thicken, then season and add acid or herbs at the end.
tips: Fond is the flavour. If the pan is clean after cooking, you either used non-stick or the heat was too low.
Butter added over high heat splits. Off the heat, whisked in cold, it emulsifies.
Add the resting juices from the meat back into the sauce.
proof: You make a glossy, well-balanced sauce in five minutes from a pan you just cooked in, without a recipe.
